newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to step into Spanish digital TV fight.
newsitem.headline: EU to step into Spanish digital TV fight.

text.p: The European Commission opened legal proceedings against Spain on Thursday, saying a law it adopted on decoders for digital and pay-TV services could restrict free trade.
The Commission stepped into a fray that has pitted the Spanish government against the opposition Socialist party and their supporting media groups for months.
It said in a statement that the law, which favours a technology known as "multicrypt", violated fundamental EU principles guaranteeing the free movement of goods and services within the EU.

Furthermore, it said Spain failed to notify the Commission before it adopted the measure as required by EU law. The Commission sent Spain a "letter of formal notice", the first step of a procedure that could lead to action before the European Court of Justice.
The Spanish law requires digital TV operators to provide compatible decoders to ensure that consumers can receive a variety of programmes using one piece of equipment.
But it says that in the absence of an agreement between companies, the multicrypt system must be adopted.
France's Canal Plus, whose decoders are based on the competing "simulcrypt" technology, complained to the Commission about the measure.
Canal Plus has teamed up with Spanish media group Prisa, which controls influential left-wing newspasper El Pais, to launch the Canalsatelite digital TV operation in Spain.

Telecommunications operators Telefonica de Espana and state television RTVE are planning to launch a rival digital package, Via Digital, in September using the multicrypt system, prompting allegations that the government is giving them time to get the project ready.
The Commission said it asked Spain to reply within 15 days. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
